components.name: Accountability Launch Ledger
components.description: Four-step causal ledger whose final wallet step keeps the irreversible click and conventional signer sources grouped together.
components.html:
1. 01

    A measured map became a human-authored model.

    Microscopy supplied the graph; engineering choices supplied the running model.

    Read the model ↗
  2. 02

    The rig decided what the cursor was trying to do.

    DOM-aware automation chose fields and inserted prewritten values.

    Inspect the loop ↗
  3. 03

    The rig completed every decisive operation.

    Automation completed the form, launch, and confirmation.

    Read its admission ↗
  4. 04

    The wallet—not the connectome—made the token exist.

    A Python-injected wallet signed and broadcast the transaction.

    Trace the click ↗Inspect the signer ↗
components.css: .ds-launch-ledger { margin:0; padding:0; color:var(--color-ink); background:var(--color-paper-bright); border-top:2px solid var(--color-ink); font-family:var(--font-body); list-style:none; } .ds-launch-ledger li { display:grid; grid-template-columns:3.5rem minmax(13rem, 0.72fr) minmax(20rem, 1.28fr) auto; gap:clamp(1rem, 3vw, 3rem); align-items:start; padding:2rem 0; border-bottom:1px solid oklch(16.6% 0.012 48 / 0.42); } .ds-launch-ledger li > span { color:var(--color-oxblood); font-family:var(--font-data); font-size:0.72rem; font-weight:700; } .ds-launch-ledger h3, .ds-launch-ledger p { margin:0; } .ds-launch-ledger h3 { font-family:var(--font-display); font-size:1.35rem; font-weight:400; line-height:1.08; } .ds-launch-ledger a { color:var(--color-civic-yellow-soft); font-size:0.86rem; font-weight:700; text-decoration-thickness:0.1em; text-underline-offset:0.2em; white-space:nowrap; } .ds-launch-ledger li > div { display:grid; gap:0.5rem; justify-items:end; } .ds-launch-ledger a:focus-visible { outline:0.125rem solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset:0.0625rem; box-shadow:0 0 0 0.375rem var(--color-focus-outer); } @media (max-width:68rem) { .ds-launch-ledger li { grid-template-columns:3.5rem minmax(13rem, 0.65fr) minmax(20rem, 1.35fr); } .ds-launch-ledger li > a, .ds-launch-ledger li > div { grid-column:3; } } @media (max-width:52rem) { .ds-launch-ledger li { grid-template-columns:2.4rem minmax(0, 1fr); gap:0.75rem 1rem; padding:1.5rem 0; } .ds-launch-ledger h3 { font-size:1.35rem; } .ds-launch-ledger p, .ds-launch-ledger li > a, .ds-launch-ledger li > div { grid-column:2; justify-items:start; } }

components.css: .ds-atlas-plate { display:grid; min-width:0; grid-template-rows:auto 1fr; margin:0; color:var(--color-paper-bright); background:var(--color-ink); border:1px solid oklch(96.5% 0.044 89.9 / 0.28); font-family:var(--font-body); } .ds-atlas-visual { padding:clamp(0.5rem, 1.8vw, 1.5rem); } .ds-atlas-visual svg { display:block; width:100%; height:auto; aspect-ratio:1; } .ds-atlas-plate figcaption { padding:clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem); color:var(--color-ink); background:var(--color-paper); border-top:0.3rem solid var(--color-civic-yellow); } .ds-atlas-plate h3 { max-width:22ch; margin:0 0 1rem; font-family:var(--font-display); font-size:clamp(1.5rem, 2.5vw, 2.2rem); font-weight:400; line-height:1.08; } .ds-atlas-plate figcaption > p { max-width:52ch; margin:0 0 1.5rem; } .ds-atlas-plate dl { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr); margin:0; border-top:1px solid oklch(16.6% 0.012 48 / 0.30); } .ds-atlas-plate dl div { min-width:0; padding:0.75rem 0.75rem 0 0; } .ds-atlas-plate dt { color:var(--color-ink-soft); font-size:0.72rem; font-weight:700; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-atlas-plate dd { margin:0; overflow-wrap:anywhere; font-family:var(--font-data); font-size:clamp(0.9rem, 1.5vw, 1.15rem); } .ds-atlas-plate a { display:inline-block; margin-top:1.5rem; color:var(--color-oxblood); font-size:0.86rem; font-weight:700; text-decoration-thickness:0.1em; text-underline-offset:0.2em; } .ds-atlas-plate a:hover { color:var(--color-ink); } .ds-atlas-plate a:focus-visible { outline:0.125rem solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset:0.0625rem; box-shadow:0 0 0 0.375rem var(--color-focus-outer); } @media (max-width:68rem) and (min-width:52.01rem) { .ds-atlas-plate { grid-template-columns:minmax(20rem, 0.9fr) minmax(20rem, 1.1fr); grid-template-rows:1fr; } .ds-atlas-plate figcaption { border-top:0; border-left:0.3rem solid var(--color-civic-yellow); } }

narrative.overview:
FLYTOWN presents public research as a town record made consequential: civic-yellow proclamations, oxblood findings, carbon ink, warm evidence paper, desk wood, stamps, pins, and ruled comparisons. The world is strange enough to hold a cigar-smoking Mayor, but exact enough that the character never masquerades as scientific proof.

The page is editorial and full-bleed, not a grid of generic product cards. Large slab-serif conclusions make the research verdict unavoidable; highly legible body copy explains its scope; monospaced measurements and provenance labels keep evidence inspectable. Material gestures are sparing and functional: paper strips lift, stamps rotate slightly, and rules connect experimental steps.

The system treats candor as the visual authority. Null findings, limits, controls, and the surviving engineering result receive the same compositional weight, so intrigue never depends on an inflated biological claim.
keyCharacteristics: Saturated civic color anchored by carbon ink and warm evidence paper.
Slab-serif proclamations, hyperlegible explanation, and mono evidence labels.
Full-width civic bands, ruled experimental flows, stamps, and ledger-like records.
Physical depth reserved for lifted paper, pinned findings, and actionable evidence.
A named illustrated Mayor who guides the story without becoming evidence.

rules.name: The Verdict Color Rule
rules.body: Civic yellow announces the public question; oxblood records the finding; carbon and paper carry the argument.

rules.name: The Provenance Is Redundant Rule
rules.body: Measured, engineering-choice, and metaphor colors must always appear with their written label; color never carries scientific meaning alone.

rules.name: The No Generic Blue Rule
rules.body: New actions and charts extend the civic, oxblood, carbon, paper, and provenance palette instead of introducing conventional product-blue accents.

rules.name: The Proclamation and Proof Rule
rules.body: Alfa Slab One states the claim, Atkinson Hyperlegible explains it, and Fragment Mono shows what can be checked.

rules.name: The Mono Means Inspectable Rule
rules.body: Do not use Fragment Mono as technological decoration; reserve it for literal data, code, identifiers, and provenance.

rules.name: The Recompose, Do Not Shrink Rule
rules.body: Responsive behavior changes the hero's layering, flow direction, tab access, and evidence grouping; it does not merely scale down desktop geometry.

rules.name: The Flat Record Rule
rules.body: Surfaces remain flat unless they behave like a lifted sheet, pinned finding, or evidence-bearing action.

rules.name: The One Desk-Lamp Rule
rules.body: Every shadow shares the same warm downward light; do not add glows, glass blur, or unrelated elevation styles.

rules.name: The Filed Edge Rule
rules.body: Public-findings components are square and ruled. Use a radius only when extending an already rounded adjacent surface, not as a default modernization pass.

dos: Do make the verdict legible in the first viewport and place scope language beside the claim.
Do use ruled flows, ledgers, stamps, and paper sheets when they clarify experimental structure.
Do keep Alfa Slab One for proclamations, Atkinson Hyperlegible for explanation, and Fragment Mono for inspectable facts.
Do recompose the hero, tabs, grids, and process flows at the documented breakpoints.
Do label measured biology, engineering choices, and metaphor in words as well as color.
Do preserve the Mayor raster's local provenance, caption, intrinsic size, and non-evidence framing.
Do preserve keyboard focus, tab semantics, reduced motion, and textual chart equivalents.
donts: Don't turn the public findings surface into pale rounded cards, glass panels, or a generic research dashboard.
Don't use the Mayor, insect vocabulary, or network imagery as evidence for a biological claim.
Don't introduce decorative monospace, unlabelled semantic color, or product-blue accents.
Don't add shadows to ordinary sections or containers that are not physically lifted evidence.
Don't shrink the desktop hero mechanically; preserve the image-backed paper-sheet composition on narrow screens.
Don't round dossier components merely because small and medium radius primitives exist elsewhere.
Don't replace or redistribute the Mayor artwork without carrying forward its authorization and provenance record.
